desc: Prove the greedy characterization: for fixed \(K\), feasibility is equivalent to pairing the \(K\) smallest selected tops with the \(K\) largest selected bottoms in increasing order.
Derive feasibility: with \(m=R-L+1\), candidate \(K\) is feasible iff \(\max_{j\in[L,L+K-1]}(P_j-j)\le m-K\), where \(P_j\) is the first index with \(A_{P_j}\ge2A_j\).
Implement the \(P_j\), \(D_j=P_j-j\), sparse-table RMQ, and per-query binary-search solution; verify the feasibility formula and run both supplied sample tests.
Identify edge cases: use integer comparison/lower_bound for \(2A_j\), sentinel \(N+1\) when no valid bottom exists, and allow answer zero for short or infeasible intervals.
Verify index/sentinel/RMQ bounds and supplied samples.
